summary: A photo-essay on heirloom family recipes, showing how dishes carry heritage across generations. It profiles seven families and their signature foods, from risotto and ackee and saltfish to tres leches cake, apple pie, lasagna, jam and chicken noodle soup. The central point is that cooking and sharing these dishes keeps families connected and their traditions alive.
one_line: Photo essay on seven families whose heirloom recipes, from risotto to chicken noodle soup, preserve heritage and connect generations.
key_facts: Grandma Lucy Thompson's spice-stained recipe scrapbook dates back to September 1948 and holds recipes from her travels, from Italy to Morocco.
Her granddaughter Amelia cooks 'Risotto alla Milanese', a saffron-infused dish served at the Thompson table every Christmas Eve since before Amelia was born.
Ackee and saltfish, Jamaica's national dish, has long been a Sunday breakfast staple for the Goodwin family.
Uncle Winston Goodwin, now in his eighties, recalls his mother making ackee and saltfish in his childhood and now teaches his grandnieces.
Maria Gonzalez's family makes Tres Leches Cake, soaked in three kinds of milk, for birthdays, graduations and weddings.
On September 19, 2023, for Maria Gonzalez's 50th birthday, her daughter Sofia continued the tres leches tradition, with three generations around the cake.
The Elliott family goes on an annual apple-picking excursion to make its guarded-secret apple pie recipe.
In the Elliott photograph, Great Aunt Edna teaches seven-year-old Jake to crimp the pie's edges.
The Ricci family's Nonna's lasagna traces back to old Naples, where Nonna learned to cook from her mother, and appears at every family event.
The Harper family's jam-making season begins each September, a tradition kept for over a century, with jars labeled with date and name.
The James family chicken noodle soup recipe was crafted during the harsh winters of the 1930s and is served whenever someone is ill.
Claire James, fresh out of surgery, was served the soup by her grandson Ethan in the photograph by Deborah Wells, dated October 30, 2023.
